terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: with an adverb
evidence: Cic. Att. 5.20.9: ā mē līberāliter tractātur
Cic. Q. fr. 2.4.5: eum nimis asperē tractat
terms.comment: Latin says how someone is treated with the verb and an adverb: līberāliter, honōrificē, asperē tractāre. Lewis & Short: “to treat, use, or conduct one’s self towards a person in any manner”.
Classically the handling of things (instruments, arms, a subject) rather than of people.

phrases.latin: … in officiō est et ā mē līberāliter tractātur
phrases.english: (Nicanor) is doing his duty, and I am treating him generously

phrases.latin: Marcellīnus autem hoc ūnō mihi quidem nōn satis facit, quod eum nimis asperē tractat
phrases.english: Marcellinus disappoints me in this one thing, that he treats him too harshly

phrases.latin: nec līberālius nec honōrificentius potuisse tractārī
phrases.english: (he wrote that) he could not have been treated more generously or more honourably

sources: Lewis & Short: tracto · Lewis & Short: tractatio
